chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il who said: He narrated to me Abu al-Hasan Zarif from Tha'laba from Aban from Ibn Abi Ya'fur

He said: I asked him about what is prohibited by breastfeeding. He said: When the infant breastfeeds until its belly is full, for that causes the growth of flesh and blood, and that is what causes prohibition. So there is no contradiction between these two narrations and the first narration which we relied upon, because his saying (peace be upon him) 'when he breastfeeds until his belly is full' is an explanation for every suckling, because it is what is considered in this chapter, rather than the meaning of the sucklings being the suckles, as many people assume, for that is what causes the growth of flesh and bone.
ai.seo_question: What is the specific condition for breastfeeding to establish prohibition in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi presents this narration to resolve the apparent discrepancy between the 'five suckles' and 'full belly' criteria by interpreting the latter as the substantive condition for establishing kinship (qarābah). It clarifies that mere mechanical suckling is insufficient; rather, the intake must be substantial enough to nourish the infant's flesh and blood, thereby integrating the physical reality of feeding with the legal threshold of prohibition.
